name: p1-refused-pulp-i2c-three-step-clear
description: Refusal sample: the PULP APB I2C target names the declaration-only behavior whose acknowledge is an ordered write/read/write clear_sequence. The declaration normalizes; this host performs one clear write, so the sequence is refused by name before any F5 case runs.
notes: This scenario exists to record the named refusal of an ordered multi-step clear, not to pass. The two-write acknowledge the current executor really performs is declared through its own scenario key (irq_clear_sequence) in configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-pulp-i2c-two-step-clear-f5.json; this file is the behavior-schema spelling, which states a three-step sequence including a read.
The refusal is raised by the behavior declaration layer (myfuzz.composition.inprocess_behavior.source_behavior) as unsupported-behavior-execution:multi_step_clear:3.
No execution is claimed: the handler in this host writes one clear word.

scl_pad_i=1 and sda_pad_i=1 are the same idle pin constants configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-i2c-zipdma-fuzz.json declares for this RTL: the APB3 register kernel refuses an unowned input, so an idle bus has to be stated before the behavior declaration is reached.
